headline: Since when did disrespecting others become a source of income, asks Mehazabien

members.title: Since when did disrespecting others become a source of income, asks Mehazabien
members.lead: Artificial intelligence (AI) is being used to create objectionable images and videos by superimposing celebrities’ faces on other people’s content. These materials are then circulated on social media. Recently, several fake videos involving actresses Mehazabien Chowdhury and Pori Moni went viral, sparking widespread discussion and criticism. Mehazabien has now spoken out against the practice, asking, “ Since when did humiliating and disrespecting another person become a way to earn money?” In a post on her Facebook page on Thursday morning, the actress expressed anger over the creation and circulation of fake content using AI. She questioned not only the conscience of those who create such material but also that of people who knowingly share it, helping it reach a wider audience. . On 13 October, objectionable videos featuring the names of Mehazabien and Pori Moni were circulated through the Instagram account of private television channel Maasranga Television. The channel later said its account had been hacked and that fake images and videos created through the misuse of AI technology had been posted. The organisation said it had recovered the account and removed the content. Fact-checking organisation Rumor Scanner investigated the incident. In a report published on Wednesday, it said the videos in question were not real. They had been created by using face-swap technology to superimpose the two actresses’ faces onto other videos. Maasranga authorities also expressed regret over the incident and said they would take legal action. Mehazabien shared her views on the issue on Thursday. At the beginning of her post, she wrote, “Creating false and fabricated content in someone’s name using AI and spreading it with the intention of humiliating them is not entertainment. It is a crime.” . However, her concern goes beyond the creation of fake content. members.title: Are we the offenders for defending ourselves, woman asks
members.lead: A 23-year-old woman who alleges that she was sexually harassed in Dhaka’s Dhanmondi area has said police at the scene did not help her, forcing her to call a relative for protection. When the relative confronted the man accused of harassing her and assaulted him, police detained the relative, who was later sentenced to 15 days in jail. “Then are we the ones who have committed a crime by trying to protect myself?” the woman asked. She made the remarks in a written message sent to Prothom Alo on Wednesday night. She said she had also posted the same statement on social media. Police detained her relative, Khalid Hasan, 35, on Wednesday afternoon over his alleged involvement in the assault of a man on a footpath in Dhanmondi. He was later produced before the Special Metropolitan Magistrate Court of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Ramna zone, which sentenced him to 15 days in jail. . On Monday afternoon, Khalid had allegedly assaulted Shahid Abdullah Al Masud, also known as Masud Rana, 48, and forced him to perform sit-ups while holding his ears. The incident took place opposite Bangladesh Eye Hospital on Satmasjid Road in Dhanmondi, following allegations of sexual harassment. Later, Dhanmondi police detained Shahid Abdullah, who was sentenced to one month in jail by the DMP’s Special Metropolitan Magistrate Court. A video of the assault went viral on social media, triggering widespread discussion and criticism. Questions were also raised about the role of two police officers present at the scene. Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Abdul Hai of Dhanmondi police station has already been withdrawn from his workplace over allegations of negligence of duty. Speaking to Prothom Alo on Wednesday, Dhanmondi police station Officer-in-Charge Muhammad Imdadul Islam Taiyeb said Abdul Hai had some responsibilities at the scene.
